overview: Three independent additions at the edges of the existing layers. A token-bucket limiter is attached to the create and redirect routes as a dependency. A destination check joins the existing URL validation in the service. Click recording gains an anonymous daily visitor identifier, produced by a dedicated privacy module, so statistics can count unique visitors and rank referrers without holding personal data.

data_model.change: ADD COLUMN visitor_hash TEXT NULL - an opaque identifier valid for one UTC day; never an address or a reversible hash of one

decisions.title: In-process token bucket
decisions.context: Abusive clients must be throttled without adding infrastructure to a single-instance service.
decisions.decision: Keep one token bucket per client address in process memory, with a hard cap on tracked clients (least recently seen evicted). Separate limiters for creation and redirects.
alternatives: A shared store such as Redis (correct across instances, but new infrastructure for a single instance)
Fixed-window counters (allow a double burst at window edges)
decisions.consequences: No new dependency and O(1) per request. Limits are per instance; moving to a shared store is required before scaling out.

decisions.title: Forwarded client address only from a declared trusted proxy
decisions.context: Behind a proxy the socket address is the proxy; but X-Forwarded-For is client-controlled, so honouring it blindly lets any client choose its own identity and bypass the limiter. (Revised after design review.)
decisions.decision: Use the socket address by default. Only when URLSHORTENER_TRUST_FORWARDED_FOR is set, use the last entry of X-Forwarded-For - the address the trusted proxy itself observed.
alternatives: Always honour the first X-Forwarded-For entry (first draft; trivially spoofable)
A configurable list of trusted proxy networks (more flexible; not needed for one proxy)
decisions.consequences: Safe by default. Deployments behind a proxy must set one flag; deployments behind several chained proxies are not supported yet.

decisions.title: Rule-based destination vetting inside URL validation
decisions.context: Confirmed scope is rule-based blocking with no external service.
decisions.decision: Reject credentials in the URL, non-public addresses in every spelling browsers accept, internal host names, the service's own host and blocklisted domains. No DNS resolution.
alternatives: Resolve the host and check the resulting address (slow, racy against DNS changes, and the service never fetches the URL anyway)
External reputation service (rejected by the product owner)
decisions.consequences: Deterministic and dependency-free. A public name that resolves to a private address is not caught; documented as a limitation.

decisions.title: Unique visitors by a keyed hash under a daily-rotating in-memory key
decisions.context: Counting distinct visitors needs an identifier that is stable for a visitor, but an unkeyed hash of an IP address is not anonymous: the IPv4 space can be enumerated in minutes, so SHA-256(ip) is personal data in disguise. (Revised after design review.)
decisions.decision: Identify a visitor as HMAC-SHA256(key, ip + user agent), where the key is random, held only in process memory and replaced every UTC day. Store the truncated digest; never store or log the key, the address or the user agent.
alternatives: Plain SHA-256 of address and user agent (first draft; reversible by enumeration)
A persistent secret salt (still links a visitor across days and becomes a secret to manage)
Cookies (changes the redirect response and needs consent)
decisions.consequences: Identifiers cannot be reversed, linked across days or recomputed after a restart. Unique counts are per day only, and a restart or a second instance over-counts slightly; accepted in exchange for holding no personal data.

decisions.title: Referrer reduced to host
decisions.context: Referrer paths and query strings regularly contain identifiers and e-mail addresses.
decisions.decision: Store only the referring host from now on; aggregate older full-URL rows by host when reading.
alternatives: Keep storing the truncated full URL (retains personal data for no product value)
decisions.consequences: Top-referrer statistics work for old and new rows. The full referrer of new clicks is no longer available, which changes one existing test on purpose.

risks.description: Rate limits throttle legitimate users who share an address (offices, mobile carriers).
risks.mitigation: Generous redirect default, configurable limits, clear 429 with Retry-After.

risks.description: The destination rules reject legitimate links.
risks.mitigation: Rules target only non-public and disguised destinations; tested against ordinary public URLs.

risks.description: Schema migration on the click log.
risks.mitigation: Additive nullable column; change-control approval before the task runs; covered by the existing upgrade tests.

risks.description: Limiter memory grows with the number of distinct clients.
risks.mitigation: Hard cap on tracked clients with least-recently-seen eviction.

risks.description: A misconfigured proxy flag lets clients spoof their address, or collapses all clients into one bucket.
risks.mitigation: Untrusted by default; only the proxy-appended entry is used; behaviour documented with the setting.

risks.description: Visitor analytics are mistaken for personal data in an audit.
risks.mitigation: Keyed, rotating, memory-only identifier; a test asserts that no address, user agent or referrer path reaches the database.

requirement_coverage.approach: Limiter dependency on POST /api/v1/links keyed by the trusted client address; RateLimited -> 429 + Retry-After
Second limiter on GET /{code}; probes and API reads have no dependency
safety.check_destination called from LinkService URL validation; UnsafeDestination -> 422
Anonymous visitor identifier stored per click; COUNT(DISTINCT) per day and referrer counts aggregated by host
privacy.VisitorHasher (HMAC, daily in-memory key) and privacy.referrer_host; no address in storage or logs
Bounded limiter state; O(1) hashing and bucket update per request
Additive response fields and nullable column; safe defaults; older referrer rows folded by host

rollback_plan: Redeploy 1.1.0: it ignores clicks.visitor_hash and the new settings. Limits and destination checks disappear with the code; no data needs repair. In this pipeline nothing reaches the target before release approval, and `sdlc rollback` restores it afterwards.
limitations: Rate limits and unique-visitor keys are per instance and reset on restart
Destination vetting does not resolve DNS
Unique-visitor counts are per day and treat several people behind one address and browser as one visitor
Only a single trusted proxy is supported for X-Forwarded-For
